Reformed Catechisms
ree-FORMD KAT-uh-kiz-uhmz
noun
From Reformed + catechism (Greek katecheo, to instruct by word of mouth); the question-and-answer manuals of Reformed instruction.

Biblical Definition

The Reformed catechisms are the question-and-answer manuals by which the Reformed churches have instructed their people, young and old, in the faith. Chief among them are the Heidelberg Catechism, with its tender opening on the believer’s only comfort in life and death, that he is not his own but belongs to his faithful Saviour Jesus Christ; the Westminster Shorter and Larger Catechisms, with the great first answer that man’s chief end is to glorify God and to enjoy Him for ever; and the Baptist Catechism, which adapts the Westminster for confessional Baptists. Catechizing follows the apostolic pattern of teaching the form of sound words and the first principles of the oracles of God, and the ancient practice of the church, which from the earliest days instructed converts and covenant children in the rudiments of the faith before the Lord’s table. The catechisms summarize the whole counsel of God—what we are to believe concerning God, and what duty God requires of man—in a form to be learned, recited, and pressed upon the heart. The dictionary honors the Reformed catechisms as a chief instrument of the church’s teaching office, a means of grounding the people in sound doctrine against the winds of error, and a treasure for the family and the church; and it laments the widespread neglect of catechizing, which leaves a generation untaught in the very rudiments of the faith.

Webster 1828 Definition

The question-and-answer manuals of Reformed instruction—Heidelberg, Westminster, the Baptist Catechism—grounding the church in sound doctrine and the duty God requires.

REFORMED CATECHISMS, the question-and-answer manuals of Reformed instruction.

Heidelberg: the believer’s only comfort is that he belongs to Christ.

Westminster: man’s chief end is to glorify God and enjoy Him for ever.

The Baptist Catechism adapts the Westminster for confessional Baptists.

A chief instrument of grounding the church in sound doctrine.

Key Scripture

2Ti 1:13 — "Hold fast the form of sound words, which thou hast heard of me, in faith and love which is in Christ Jesus."

Deu 6:7 — "And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up."

Heb 5:12 — "For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat."

Luk 1:4 — "That thou mightest know the certainty of those things, wherein thou hast been instructed."

Modern Corruption

Catechizing is dismissed as cold rote or sterile tradition; Scripture commends the diligent teaching of sound words and first principles to old and young.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The corruption is the modern dismissal of catechizing as cold rote learning, dead formality, or sterile tradition that quenches living faith. This judgment mistakes the form for the substance. The catechisms are not meant to replace heart-religion but to ground it; the memorized answer becomes a lamp the believer carries through life, a settled summary of truth to steady him when error blows and trials come. Many a saint has found the catechism’s words on his lips in the hour of death.

The principle to recover is the duty and blessing of catechetical instruction. Scripture commands the diligent teaching of God’s truth to children (Deu 6:7), the holding fast of the form of sound words (2 Tim 1:13), and the grounding of believers in the first principles of the oracles of God (Heb 5:12); Luke wrote his Gospel that Theophilus might know the certainty of the things wherein he had been instructed—catechized (Luke 1:4). The neglect of catechizing has left a generation untaught in the very rudiments of the faith, easy prey to every error. The Reformed catechisms remain a chief instrument of the church’s teaching office, a treasure for family and church, to be recovered, not despised.

Hebrew Roots

Reformed + catechism (Greek katecheo, to instruct by mouth); the question-and-answer manuals grounding the church in sound doctrine and duty.

Reformed catechisms — the question-and-answer manuals of instruction.

Heidelberg, Westminster Shorter and Larger, and the Baptist Catechism.

Follow the apostolic pattern of teaching the form of sound words (2Ti 1:13).

Ground old and young in the first principles of the oracles (Heb 5:12).

A treasure for family and church, widely and wrongly neglected.
